newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African consumer confidence eases in Q1 - survey.
newsitem.headline: S.African consumer confidence eases in Q1 - survey.

text.p: Consumer confidence slipped in the first quarter of this year and was expected to continue slackening for at least another six months, the University of Stellenbosch's Bureau for Economic Research said on Tuesday.
"This decline interrupts the upward trend in the level of consumer confidence in the last two quarters of 1996," BER said in a statement.
This meant that consumer confidence was now back at the levels seen in the second quarter of 1996, but it still remained relatively high.
It said the lower consumer confidence was mainly due to the fact that the most recent survey was the first undertaken after the rise in the prime overdraft and mortgage bond rate in November 1996.

In addition, for the first time in several quarters, low income earners had lower expectations of improving their financial position, although fewer high income earners expected their financial position to deteriorate over the next 12 months.
Low income earners saw less chance of improving their income because they were the worst affected by job losses and the prospect of finding formal sector employment remained "very bleak".
They had also not received expected large wage increases.

"The decline in the level of consumer confidence and the expectations about sales during the second quarter of retailers, wholesalers and new vehicle dealers point to a further slackening in the growth rate of private consumption expenditure over the next six months.

"The growth rate in private consumption expenditure (measured year-on-year) could pick up towards the end of 1997 as real disposable income posts higher growth and the banks lower interest rates," it said.
